  "paraphrased_article": "She is a clairvoyant and the daughter of one of Europe’s longest-reigning monarchs; he is a Californian who calls himself a sixth-generation shaman. When Princess Märtha Louise of Norway wed Durek Verrett on Saturday afternoon, it was far from a typical royal wedding – yet crowds still gathered along the grey, clouded streets of Geiranger hoping to see the bride. 

Princess Märtha Louise, the only daughter of King Harald and Queen Sonja and 52 years old, is fourth in the Norwegian line of succession. She and the 49-year-old Verrett were married in a traditional Church of Norway ceremony, with royals and celebrities in attendance, at the four-star Hotel Union in a small village nestled beneath the Geiranger fjord. 

The princess was accompanied by seven bridesmaids, among them her teenage daughters Leah and Emma Behn from her first marriage to the late Norwegian writer Ari Behn, whom she divorced in 2017. The roughly 350 guests included her brother, Crown Prince Haakon, and his wife, Crown Princess Mette-Marit; Sweden’s Crown Princess Victoria and her husband, Prince Daniel; as well as Prince Constantijn and Princess Laurentien of the Netherlands. 

Märtha Louise has long led a life outside traditional royal expectations, having publicly identified as a clairvoyant and run a healing school for about a decade where she said she taught participants to communicate with angels. In 2022, she announced she would withdraw from formal royal duties to concentrate on the business she runs with Verrett and to draw a clearer line between their ventures and the Norwegian royal household. 

Verrett describes himself on Instagram as a “servant of God” and “energy activator”. Among the prominent people he has worked with is Goop founder Gwyneth Paltrow, whom he has referred to as his “soul sister”."
}
```
